what: Zero-shot Meta Omnilingual ASR model cards on the real-voice clips (30 sentences per language, cut per sentence)
package: omnilingual-asr 0.2.0, fairseq2 0.6, torch 2.8.0 cu128, bf16 (pipeline default)
cer_method: judge.cer(' '.join(refs), ' '.join(hyps)); cer_pooled = per-clip edits summed / reference chars
gpu_note: Measured on one NVIDIA H200 (RunPod, EUR-IS-4); A100/H100 had no stock
decoder_note: Every LLM card has the same ~1.3 B-parameter decoder (LLM params minus the CTC card of the same size); only the encoder grows

l4_estimate.method: estimate, not measured on an L4. H200 batch-1 RTF is ~0.08-0.09 for every LLM size (per-step overhead, not weight reads). On an L4 (24 GB, ~300 GB/s, ~120 TFLOPS bf16) the decoder step is bandwidth-bound: ~2.6 GB of bf16 decoder weights per token is ~9 ms; at 8.5-13 tokens per audio second (ht/lo/km, counted with the cards' tokenizers) that is ~0.08-0.12 s per audio second, plus the encoder (one pass, ~0.01-0.07 s/s from 300M to 7B). Expected L4 RTF ~0.15-0.25 for 300M and ~0.2-0.35 for 7B per stream: real time either way, with less headroom for 4 streams at 7B.
l4_estimate.memory: peak bf16 at batch 1: 3.6 GB (LLM 300M) to 15.1 GB (LLM 7B); batch 16: 5.5 to 17.4 GB. All fit 24 GB with VoxLingua LID and Silero VAD beside them.

not_run.omniASR_LLM_Unlimited_{300M,1B,3B,7B}_v2: long-form variants; queued last, but results were lost when the pod was deleted before they were copied back
not_run.omniASR_LLM_7B_ZS: zero-shot card for unseen languages; needs in-context example audio/text pairs (transcribe_with_context), so not comparable
not_run.omniASR_W2V_*: pretrained encoders without an ASR head

endpointing_sweep.what: omni-stt's own Segmenter (Silero VAD at the pinned ref, AudioIn 96 ms blocks) over the FULL real-voice clips, each segment decoded by the service's decode path; CER on the joined text vs the 30 reference sentences
endpointing_sweep.service_ref: translation-open-stack omni checkout 1e139b9 (services/omni-stt/server.py + server/), omnilingual-asr 0.1.0 / fairseq2 0.6 / torch 2.8.0 per constraints.txt (the service's pins), bf16
endpointing_sweep.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition MIG 1g.24gb (RunPod EUR-IS-2, $0.69/h); L4, 3090 and 4090 had no stock
endpointing_sweep.level_note: The clips join FLEURS recordings made at very different gains: km has 5 sentences peaking near -42 dBFS, en 23 of 30 under -30 dBFS. Silero hears none of the quietest, so the Segmenter drops them whole (km: 4 sentences, en: 3). 'levelled' scales each sentence to RMS 2000 (int16; peak capped at -1 dBFS) before the VAD, as a microphone with AGC would deliver it; that isolates the endpointing settings.
endpointing_sweep.columns: see score_sweep.py: seg_wait = emit - end of last speech block for pause-ended turns (the endpoint wait, audio time); sent_wait = per sentence, emit of the first segment reaching its speech end minus that end; mid_cuts = segment boundaries inside a sentence; dropped = sentences the VAD did not hear; decode_s_p90 = GPU decode wall time per segment

per_sentence_baseline.note: the 'runs' above: clips cut per sentence, omnilingual-asr 0.2.0, H200
